title: Discount Benefit
description: The structured shape of a discount: what it gives, typed by `type`. One shared model for the common discount shapes, reusable wherever a discount is described, whether it is an offer not yet applied or the attribution of one that was. Well-known types: `amount_off` (carries `amount`), `percent_off` (carries `basis_points`, optionally capped by `max_amount`), `fixed_price` (carries `price`), `free_shipping`, and `free_item` (optionally carries `quantity` and `item`). The vocabulary is open. A consumer that does not recognize `type` MUST NOT derive any amount from the benefit; it MAY still present the human-readable fields of the object that embeds it.

type.description: Benefit kind. Well-known values: `amount_off`, `percent_off`, `fixed_price`, `free_shipping`, `free_item`. Businesses MAY use reverse-domain names for custom kinds (e.g., `com.example.benefit.gift_wrap`). Unknown values MUST be tolerated and establish no price inference.

amount.description: For `amount_off`: the amount taken off, greater than zero. Mutually exclusive with `basis_points` and `price`.

basis_points.description: For `percent_off`: the percentage taken off, in basis points (hundredths of a percent; `1250` = 12.5%). Mutually exclusive with `amount` and `price`.

max_amount.description: Cap on a `basis_points` benefit: the most it takes off in total. Omitted means no cap. Requires `basis_points`.

price.description: For `fixed_price`: what each unit the benefit applies to costs while it applies. Mutually exclusive with `amount` and `basis_points`.

quantity.description: For `free_item`: the number of units given free.

item.title: Free Item
item.description: For `free_item`: the item given free, when it is a specific gift. Omitted means the free units are among the items the benefit applies to (e.g., 'buy two, get one free'), chosen by the Business.

id.description: Identifier of the gift in the Business's catalog, when it can be looked up.

value.description: What the gift is worth, for presentation.
